methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $690M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Bethlehem Steel Corp is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $690M to date. The valuation universe comprises 10 same-sector peers: one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting narrow filter criteria, limiting the applicability of traditional peer-median approaches.

Given data constraints, the valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total raised ($690M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 1.2x multiplier to reflect the step-up from Growth to the subsequent stage, this method implies a valuation of $828M. This approach assumes typical venture scaling patterns but carries inherent limitations absent direct comparable transaction data.

The triangulated valuation range is $704M to $952M, with a median of $828M, derived from a single methodology. The narrow methodological base reflects insufficient granular peer data at comparable stage and scale. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.2x stage multiplier absent company-specific metrics (revenue, growth rate, unit economics), and the representativeness of the broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector given the heterogeneity of business models. Additional transaction or financial disclosure data would strengthen conviction in this range.
